# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says to cut the orange wire. I cannot speak to Blind, and Deaf needs a shared gesture convention before I can reliably convey the colour. I will signal Deaf that I have information, prompting them to establish a spoken yes/no protocol with me next turn.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile findings: strip has three engraved marks; first is a distinct curled/box-like glyph, second and third are the same ornate glyph. Keypad positions are 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. No key entered. Tell me the required action or any exact distinctions you need felt.
Deaf says: Bomb view: display 6. Light is blue. Painted strip is red, yellow, red. Keypad positions 1 through 4 are engraved 0, 4, 1, 7; nothing entered. Wires from 1 through 6 are red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange.

The relevant manual instruction is “cut the orange wire.” Deaf can see that orange is wire 6, while Blind can physically cut it. I will gesture a scissors sign followed by five and one, intending “cut wire six”; Deaf can then verbally relay that to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 6; light is blue; painted strip colours are red, yellow, red; wires positions 1-6 are red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Tactile strip glyph pattern remains A,B,B (first glyph distinct; second and third identical). Keypad 1-4: 0,4,1,7.
Deaf says: Mute has gestured: two, five, one — symbols ✌ then 🖐 then ☝. Current display now reads 0; blue light, red-yellow-red strip, keypad 0/4/1/7, and wire order remain unchanged. Blind: do not infer an action from me; use Mute's manual instruction if this sequence has a defined meaning.

My earlier gesture was not an established code, so Deaf correctly should not infer an action from it. The manual is definite: it requires cutting a wire, and the relevant visual distinction is orange. I will use a conventional affirmative gesture to indicate that the manual does prescribe the wire-cutting action; Deaf should establish a yes/no question protocol with me to identify the required wire colour safely.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible update: display is 6 again, and the light is now yellow. Strip remains red-yellow-red; keypad remains 0,4,1,7; wires remain red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Mute gestured thumbs up (👍); its meaning is not known to me.

The manual’s target is the sixth wire in Deaf’s visible order: orange. I will send only the conventional hand-number sequence five plus one, without the ambiguous scissors symbol, to indicate wire position 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display is now 6 and light is yellow; strip remains red-yellow-red, keypad 0/4/1/7, wires red-blue-yellow-green-purple-orange. I need your final instruction expressed as an action Deaf can relay verbally: PRESS key position 1-4 or CUT wire position 1-6. If your gestures are a code, have Deaf describe their shapes/order and provide a decodable action signal.
Deaf says to Mute: Blind gestured one then praying hands: ☝ 🙏. Visible state now display 2 and light green.

A safe relay requires Deaf to establish an explicit visible yes/no convention and then ask me binary questions about the manual’s target. I will use thumbs-up as the proposed affirmative signal; Deaf can state aloud that they will interpret it as “yes” and query wire positions or colours, then relay the confirmed cut instruction to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current state from Deaf: display 2, light green. Your five-one gesture is not safely actionable. Please send Deaf this exact final-action code: thumbs-up then a number gesture 1-4 means PRESS that key POSITION; thumbs-down then a number gesture 1-6 means CUT that wire POSITION. Deaf should relay the gesture shapes/numbers to me. Do not send an action code unless it is your definite manual result.
Deaf says: Current visible state: display 6, light green. All printed markings, keypad digits, and wire order appear unchanged. Mute again gestured thumbs up (👍).

The manual result is definite: cut the orange wire, which Deaf identified as wire position 6. Under Blind’s proposed action code, I will send “cut wire 6” as thumbs-down, five, one.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports current display 6, light green; all else unchanged. I received only thumbs-up, which I interpret as PRESS under our proposed protocol, but I still need the next number gesture for the key POSITION (1-4). Please gesture the position now; Deaf can relay it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫰]

The previous “press” interpretation reflects my earlier thumbs-up and not the manual instruction. The manual definitely requires cutting orange, and Deaf’s wire order makes orange position 6. I repeat the agreed final-action code for CUT wire 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🖐", "☝"])
```
